title: One Question Each · Pair relay
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play One Question Each · Pair relay with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: The lead writes a familiar object on a hidden slip. Every other player asks one yes-or-no question; with two players, the partner may ask three. The group identifies the object after the questions. Form pairs. On each pair’s turn, both people make separate attempts with fresh challenges, helping only their partner. The pair earns one point only if both succeed. Each pair has two turns. Highest score wins.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4, 6 or 8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In One Question Each, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The group identifies the object after the questions.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
recall.why: The group identifies the object after the questions.
